newsitem.title: UK: British Gas backs off in UK tax wrangle.
newsitem.headline: British Gas backs off in UK tax wrangle.

text.p: A tax wrangle between British Gas and the British government came to an end on Tuesday as the utility said it would not proceed with legal action for repayment of gas levy after having earlier claimed it was overcharged.
"The company is now satisfied that the gas levy legislation has been applied correctly and will therefore not be pursuing its claim," British Gas said.

The dispute between British Gas and the Department of Trade and Industry (DT) became public in July when the utility announced it had issued a writ to recover "substantial" amounts of money from the government.

The DTI said earlier British Gas claimed to have paid about 1.0 billion stg ($1.65 billion) too much under the gas levy act, which was introduced in 1981. The levy currently obliges British Gas to pay four pence per therm of gas delivered to beach terminals from North Sea gas fields.
"I am pleased that the matter has been put to rest without the need to resort to litigation," energy minister Lord Fraser said.
British Gas had taken out the writ, which was never in fact served on the DTI, to keep open the opportunity of bringing the dispute to court if no out-of-court agreement could be reached.
The tax dispute focused on eight fields and 24 contracts between the utility and exploration firms.
To cover its position, the DTI responded in July by taking out writs against the gas producers so it could claim back money from them just in case British Gas would have to be repaid.
But the precautionary proceedings against the producers have now been dropped after the dispute with British Gas has been settled, the DTI said.
"We will not now have to proceed with the action against the producers which has been undertaken on a contingency basis to protect the taxpayer," Lord Fraser said in a statement.
British Gas, meanwhile, is still in talks with gas producers to renegotiate so called "take-or-pay" contracts, which oblige it to buy gas well above spot prices even if it cannot find a market.
The company's efforts to be repaid gas levy were earlier seen by analysts as another way of trying to soften the negative impact of the restrictive take-or-pay deals.

But the DTI said the gas levy matter was now completely closed. "There were never any negotiations with British Gas because there was nothing to negotiate and as to what is happening with the levy in the future: there is no action that we are taking on it," a ministry spokesman said.
Separately, British Gas announced that Harry Moulson had resigned from the board and relinquished his post as managing director of its TransCo pipeline unit due to medical reasons.
David Varney, executive director of British Gas, will act as temporarily as manging director of the unit.
British Gas shares eased 1-1/2 pence to 191-1/2 by 1245 GMT. ($1=.6050 Pound)
